specs.heading: Arms Warrior Stat Priority in WoW Forever
specs.intro: Given that the beta was level-locked at Level 30, it's unclear not only what stats are important for Arms Warrior, but also the availability of stats at Level 60. The priority below is purely speculative for endgame and is based on what we know from beta testing, but has not been tested in-game at Level 60.
notes: No separate leveling list.
Author rule of thumb: an item with 1.5 times more Agility than Strength may yield more DPS; breakpoint depends on total Strength and Crit.
Hit above 8% still has value (white hits) but ranks below Crit.
Weapon Skill is discussed in the body (glancing-blow table) but is not in the numbered priority list.
Impale raises ability crits to 220%. Crit Cap is mentioned as dynamic with Hit; it does not limit racial or ability crit.

specs.author: Riyani
specs.heading: Protection Warrior Stat Priority in WoW Forever — Defensive Priority
specs.intro: In everything from gearing, talents, and rotation, you should think of the balance between defensiveness and offensive throughput/threat as a spectrum, and it's seldom wise to be on either end of that spectrum. As such, when we look at a stat priority, we have to be a bit cautious when we say outline which stats to pursue. Below, you have the best stat priorities for a Defensive, Balanced, and Offensive build, which will be the correct option for your party/raid may be different from other Warriors, but starting with a more balanced approach will be a good idea.
notes: Three profiles on one page. Author recommends starting with Balanced.
No separate numbered leveling list. Spirit is called useful while leveling.

Rough single-target equivalences (Deep Protection Impale build): 1% Expertise before soft cap = 115 AP; 1% Hit before melee cap = 60 AP; 1% Expertise after soft cap before hard cap = 46 AP; 1% Crit = 34 AP; 1% Haste = 21 AP.
Defense cap is 440 total Defense (unclear how necessary it will be in Forever). Expertise soft cap 6.5%, hard cap 14%; value past 6% is cut in half, past 14% is 0.
Melee/spell hit caps vs enemy level: 60: 5%/4%; 61: 5.5%/6%; 62: 6%/11%; 63: 8%/17%. Spell hit is not worth pursuing (except Taunt).
Author warns not to be dogmatic; efficiently itemized threat pieces (e.g. Lionheart Helm) can beat a 'tank-looking' item.

specs.heading: Retribution Paladin Stat Priority in WoW Forever
specs.intro: The priority below is built from the data we have based on the beta. Expect it to shift once Level 60 dungeon and raid gear is available.

caps.Hit Chance: 9% (safe melee target vs raid bosses; body notes sources disagree on whether Classic hit suppression was removed, and spells have a 16% miss vs a level-63 boss, but Seals/Judgement are melee so only the melee cap is needed)

Weapon is by far the most important item. Shockadin / Seal of Righteousness wants a faster two-hander; otherwise prefer slower two-handers. First +5 Weapon Skill is called the most valuable PvE breakpoint (up to 3% hit); first +8 reduces glancing penalty.

Author comment on the same page (not in the list): "I'm aware of the recent major reworks to Retribution Paladin and am working on updating the guide as soon as possible to reflect that information and the latest theorycrafting." Page last updated 2026-10-31, so this list may be pending a rewrite.
Champion of the Light currently converts 60% of Intellect to Spell Power at 3/3; author says this may change again.
Haste is discussed in the body as traditionally strong but 'more testing is required' and is not on the numbered list.

specs.author: L0uki
specs.heading: Feral Druid Tank Stat Priority in WoW Forever — Defensive Priority
specs.intro: With limited information at hand about level 60 content, definite stat priorities cannot be established. That said, the priorities listed below offer a safe, reliable starting point suited to a wide range of encounters and scenarios. The defensive priorities emphasize a druid's ability to build up a huge effective health pool, which is further embellished by reaching 440 defense, effectively preventing critical strikes. This gearing approach limits worst-case events while accepting slightly worse average-case performance. Similarly, the offensive priority seeks to limit misses, dodges, and parries before stacking straight damage: since many of our abilities carry a threat modifier, the raw value matters less---as long as the ability connects.
notes: Separate page from Feral DPS (Cat). Defensive and Offensive lists only — no Balanced list.
No separate numbered leveling list. Spell Power is called a niche leveling/dungeon benefit via Thorns, not pursued at max level.

Hit aim is the 8% melee cap. Expertise soft cap 6.5% (dodge), hard cap 14% (parry). Armor is useful up to the armor cap of 17,265. Weapon speed is largely irrelevant (Bear Form is a fixed 2.5s before Haste).
Offensive list item 6 and item 8 are both 'Strength' on the live page. Recorded verbatim; likely a typo.

notes: No separate leveling list. Author says the real job is balancing throughput vs mana, and this ranked list focuses on throughput first because consumables and cooldowns can cover mana. Do not ignore mana stats; a big mana gain for a small Spell Healing loss can still be an upgrade.

specs.author: Lucenia
specs.heading: Elemental Shaman Stat Priority in WoW Forever
specs.intro: Our end-game stat priority is roughly

caps.Hit Chance: 17% (up to 5% from Tidal Focus, rest from gear)

notes: This is labeled an end-game priority. Strength is explicitly '(Only while leveling)'. Author: there isn't necessarily one right answer for how to gear while leveling; find a balance that feels good.
Unusual among casters: Spell Piercing and Haste are listed above Hit and Spell Damage.

Body: Elemental ST damage is roughly 70% Nature / 30% Fire; cleave/AoE closer to 40% Nature / 60% Fire. Elemental Fury raises crits to 200%. 10 Spell Piercing vs no resistance adds about 1.8% damage on average at level 60. Haste/Cast Speed stack multiplicatively; GCD floors at 1 second.
Body says spells have a 17% chance to miss against bosses (other caster pages sometimes say 16% then cap at 17%).

specs.author: Voulk
specs.heading: Discipline Priest Stat Priority in WoW Forever
specs.intro: The beta was level-locked at Level 30 and we did not get to see any endgame content so there are still some outlying questions in regards to which stats will be best and which ones will even be available. This guide therefore includes a lot of speculation for now, though it will be quickly updated shortly after the game goes live.
notes: No separate numbered leveling list. Body: Spell Power is particularly good while leveling (you spend a lot of time DPSing even as a healer) and less relevant for endgame, where you'd rather have Healing Power.
Author: balance throughput vs mana fight-by-fight; for now aim to get a lot of Healing Power, Intellect, and Spirit. More refined comparisons at level 60.

Heals don't need Hit. When DPS is valuable, cap via Holy Precision rather than Hit on gear. Haste is mentioned in the body (rare; GCD/cast floor 1s; does not affect HoT tick rate) but is not on the list.
Crit bonuses: Divine Aegis (15% shield) and Renewed Hope (reduces Weakened Soul duration).

specs.author: Spanklord
specs.heading: Holy Priest Stat Priority in WoW Forever
specs.intro: Given that the beta was level-locked at Level 30, it's unclear not only what stats are ultimately going to be the most important for Holy Priest, but also the general availability of specific stats at Level 60. The priority below is purely speculative for endgame and is based on what we know from beta testing, but has not been tested in-game at Level 60.
notes: No separate leveling list. Spell Hit is explicitly not relevant (heals do not miss).

In Forever, bonus healing also includes one-third as much bonus damage (a Forever change). Spiritual Guidance at 5 points increases spell healing by up to 25% of total Spirit and spell damage by up to 8% of total Spirit (Classic gave 25% to both).

Author treats MP5 and Spirit as roughly equal depending on content: MP5 works during chain pulls; Spirit is more available below high-tier gear. Note: Renew cannot critically strike. Inspiration (armor buff on crit heals) is the main reason to take Spell Crit.
Body formula for Spirit regen while casting uses a 0.15 multiplier 'assuming 3/3 Meditation'; 3/3 Meditation is normally 50%. Flag this as a possible typo on the page, not used in the priority list.

specs.author: Zephan
specs.heading: Affliction Warlock Stat Priority in WoW: Forever
specs.intro: This order comes from level 60 stat weights in Warlock simulation tools for the Wrack raid build. The SM Ruin build uses the same order.
verbatim: 3. Hit Chance (up to 12% from gear with 5/5 Suppression)

caps.Hit Chance: 12% from gear and buffs with 5/5 Suppression (17% total; 4% vs same-level targets)

notes: Most recently updated page of the set (2026-11-11). Unlike most Wowhead Forever lists, this one is explicitly from level-60 sim weights, not only a beta estimate. No Stamina on the list. No separate leveling list.
Author-stated sim equivalences: Wrack build 1% Crit ≈ 9 SP, 1% Hit ≈ 7.5 SP, 1% Haste ≈ 2.5 SP, 1 Spell Pierce ≈ 1.25 SP. SM Ruin: 1% Crit ≈ 11 SP, 1% Hit ≈ 9 SP, 1% Haste ≈ 6.5 SP.

DoT ticks can crit. Pandemic (DoTs/drains/Wrack) and Ruin (Shadow Bolt/Immolate) make almost every crit deal double damage. Haste does not speed DoT ticks, DoT durations, or channeled Wrack/Drain Life. Spell Pierce is 1/10th as effective on DoTs. Past the Hit cap, swap Hit for Spell Power or Crit.

notes: No separate leveling list. No Stamina on the list. Same skeleton as Affliction, with Fire school damage.

Author: + Fire Damage is worth about two-thirds of Spell Power; + Shadow Damage about a third. 1% Crit and 1% Hit are nearly tied at roughly 9 SP, Crit slightly ahead. 1% Haste ≈ 7 SP. Past the Hit cap, swap Hit for Spell Power or Crit.
Raid build takes 5/5 Ruin and 3/3 Pandemic. Haste does not speed DoT ticks or the demon.

specs.author: warstry
specs.heading: Assassination Rogue Stat Priority in WoW Forever
specs.intro: Given that the beta was level-locked at Level 30, it's unclear not only what stats are important for Assassination Rogue, but also the availability of stats at Level 60. The priority below is purely speculative for endgame and is based on what we know from beta testing, but has not been tested in-game at Level 60.

caps.Hit Chance (dual-wield white): 27% (mentioned in the body, not as a numbered rank)

notes: All three Rogue specs share the same numbered list and nearly the same accompanying paragraph. Assassination uniquely stresses Hit up to the 17% poison cap and values Crit more because of Seal Fate. Combat's Haste section also mentions Blade Flurry. Combat is reviewed by Simonize.
No separate numbered leveling list. Spirit is called moderately valuable while leveling (out-of-combat health regen) with no combat benefit.

Main-hand weapon DPS is called the biggest damage factor but is not itself a numbered list item (unlike Ret and Feral). Auto-attack Hit still has some value up to the 27% dual-wield cap, below the other caps.

Crit and Haste are 'currently equal in value,' with Haste likely much harder to find. Haste does not increase Energy regen. 29 Agility = 1% physical Crit; Agility does not convert to Poison Crit, but secondary Crit on items does.
Assassination uniquely emphasizes Hit through the 17% poison cap because of heavy Poison damage, and values Crit more than the other Rogue specs due to Seal Fate.

specs.heading: Beast Mastery Hunter Stat Priority in WoW Forever
specs.intro: Given that the beta was level-locked at Level 30, it's unclear not only what stats are important for Beast Mastery Hunter, but also the availability of stats at Level 60. The priority below is purely speculative for endgame and is based on what we know from beta testing, but has not been tested in-game at Level 60.
notes: No separate leveling list. Marksmanship uniquely says this list 'ranks every stat per 1% or 1 point, depending on how they show up on gear.' BM and Survival do not repeat that sentence but use the same '% Hit' / '% Crit' wording for the first two ranks.
Body Hit target is 9% so yellow hits never miss on skull-level bosses; also covers normal ranged and two-handed white hits. One-hand whites need more Hit.

Careful Aim converts Intellect to ranged Attack Power 1-to-1. Body Agility bullets say '1 Agility = 1 ranged Attack Power' immediately after prose that says Hunters gain 2 ranged Attack Power per point of Agility — an internal inconsistency on the page.
Strength is discussed in the body as only slightly useful for melee weaving and is not on the BM list (unlike Survival).
Bestial Discipline lets mana regen continue while casting.
